journal.text: First session, starting from $50k cash with no prior positions. Market context: broad tech/growth selloff over the past month (NVDA, TSLA, AVGO, MSFT, GOOGL all down meaningfully from mid-Feb highs), elevated volatility. Given the lack of any track record and uncertain near-term macro backdrop, I'm deploying only ~45% of capital into a diversified starter basket of quality large caps that have pulled back to more reasonable levels, spanning mega-cap tech (MSFT, AAPL, GOOGL, AVGO, QCOM) and defensive/staples names (COST, PEP, LIN, ADP, WMT) for ballast. Keeping over half the account in cash as a buffer to add opportunistically on further weakness or rotate if trends stabilize/reverse. No single position exceeds ~6% of NAV. Will reassess next session using fresh closes to judge whether the downtrend is stabilizing or extending; would add more aggressively on signs of basing/reversal, or trim/hedge further if declines accelerate broadly.

Holding all positions unchanged today. April 1 saw a broad bounce across tech (MSFT, AAPL, GOOGL, AVGO, META, AMZN, NVDA, TSLA all up 1-4%) after weeks of steady declines, but a single green day after a multi-week downtrend isn't enough evidence of a durable reversal, especially with elevated volatility and macro uncertainty (tariff headlines) still in play. Current allocation (~45% invested across mega-cap tech + defensive staples, ~55% cash) reflects appropriate caution for a brand-new account with no track record. Will reassess as more closes come in: if the bounce extends 2-3 more sessions with reduced volatility, I'll deploy more cash into the existing basket or add further diversification (e.g., healthcare/semis). If declines resume and break below March 31 lows on volume, I may trim risk further or rotate into cash/defensives. No new capital deployed this session; waiting for clearer trend confirmation.

Bounce from the March 31 lows has now extended two sessions (Apr 1, Apr 2) across the whole basket - MSFT, AAPL, GOOGL, COST, LIN, ADP, AVGO, QCOM, WMT all posted gains both days, with AVGO/QCOM/COST showing particularly strong follow-through. Per my plan from 4/2, a 2-3 session bounce warrants modest incremental deployment rather than full conviction, since daily ranges (esp. in AVGO, TSLA-adjacent semis, COST) remain wide and macro/tariff headline risk is still unresolved. Adding a small, equal $500 tranche to each of the 10 existing positions (~$5k total) increases invested exposure from ~45% to ~55% of NAV while preserving a substantial (~45%) cash buffer for either further opportunistic buying on dips or defensive flexibility if the bounce fails. No new names added - staying within the proven quality/defensive basket until trend clarity improves. Will reassess next session: continued gains with narrowing ranges -> keep scaling in; a reversal back below the March 31 closing lows on volume -> pause deployment and consider trimming.

April 3 close data shows a severe, broad selloff that decisively breaks below the March 31 lows on elevated volume - AAPL -9.2%, AVGO -10.5%, QCOM -9.5% in a single session, far exceeding normal daily ranges. This is the exact 'reversal below March 31 lows on volume' trigger I flagged in my 4/3 journal as a signal to pause deployment and trim risk. Notably the damage is concentrated in hardware/semis names with heavy import/export and China exposure (AAPL, AVGO, QCOM), while defensive staples (PEP, COST, WMT, ADP, LIN) and services-heavy MSFT/GOOGL held up comparatively better (down 0-4%), consistent with a tariff-driven shock rather than a generic risk-off move. Given the size and abruptness of the move, I'm not chasing this dip with fresh buying - instead trimming ~35-40% of the three most tariff-exposed, highest-beta positions (AAPL, AVGO, QCOM) to reduce concentration risk and raise cash buffer back toward ~50% of NAV. Keeping MSFT, GOOGL, COST, PEP, LIN, ADP, WMT positions intact since they've shown relative resilience and represent the more defensive core of the basket. This is a risk-reduction move, not a full exit - if the shock proves short-lived and tariff headlines de-escalate with names stabilizing/basing over the next few sessions, I'd look to redeploy into AAPL/AVGO/QCOM at better levels. If declines continue or broaden into the defensive names too, I'll trim further and raise more cash.

April 4 close data confirms the selloff broadened decisively beyond the tariff-exposed hardware names into the 'defensive' core of the basket: LIN -6.7%, ADP -6.7%, WMT -4.6%, PEP -3.1%, COST -5.2%, MSFT -3.6%, GOOGL -3.5% - all in a single session on markedly elevated volume (WMT 36M vs ~20M avg, MSFT 49M vs ~18M avg, AAPL 126M vs ~35M avg). This is exactly the 'broadening decline' scenario I flagged on 4/4 as the trigger to trim further and raise more cash, since it indicates a market-wide risk-off/liquidation event rather than an isolated tariff-sector rotation - no name in the basket was spared. Trimming ~25% of every remaining position (including the previously-untouched defensive names) rather than concentrating cuts in semis/hardware, since the damage this time hit everything roughly proportionally. This raises cash from ~53% to ~65% of NAV, preserving capital and dry powder while trend/volatility remains extreme and no basing/stabilization signal has appeared yet (still making lower lows with expanding ranges, not narrowing). Not adding any new positions or names - staying in raise-cash/wait mode. I will look to redeploy into this quality basket once I see 2-3 consecutive sessions of gains or flat action with contracting daily ranges and volume normalizing toward pre-selloff levels, signaling the panic/liquidation phase has passed. If declines continue at this pace, I will continue trimming toward a higher cash floor (75-80%) to protect capital through the crash.

April 7 close data shows an extraordinarily volatile single session across the basket - huge intraday reversals (AAPL traded 174.62-194.15 before closing 181.46, MSFT 344.79-371 before closing 357.86, AVGO 138.10-160.43 closing 154.14) on very heavy volume, following the broad capitulation-style decline confirmed on 4/4. This kind of huge-range reversal day (sharp gap down, strong intraday rally, still closing mixed vs prior day) is often associated with panic/capitulation lows, but it is only ONE session - my stated redeployment trigger from 4/7 requires 2-3 consecutive sessions of gains/flat action WITH CONTRACTING ranges and normalizing volume, which has clearly not happened yet (ranges are still expanding, not contracting, and volume remains 2-3x normal). Staying in wait mode: holding current ~65% cash buffer and existing trimmed positions unchanged, no new buys or sells today. This avoids both chasing a potentially false bounce and panic-selling into what could be a bottoming process. I will watch the next 1-2 sessions closely: if gains continue with narrowing daily ranges and volume falling back toward pre-selloff levels (~15-20M for MSFT, ~35-40M for AAPL), I'll begin redeploying cash into the basket incrementally. If instead we see another sharp leg down through the 4/7 lows on volume, I'll trim further toward a 75-80% cash floor.

April 8 close data still shows unresolved volatility and continued net declines across most of the basket: AAPL -5.0%, QCOM -3.9%, WMT -2.4%, PEP -2.0%, LIN -2.9%, ADP -1.6%, GOOGL -1.4%, MSFT -0.9%, only COST (+0.07%) and AVGO (+1.2%) squeaked out gains. Daily ranges remain very wide (AAPL 169-190, MSFT 350-374, LIN 409-433) and volume is still running 2-4x normal (AAPL 120M vs ~35M avg, MSFT 36M vs ~18M avg). This does not meet my stated redeployment trigger of 2-3 consecutive sessions of gains/flat action with CONTRACTING ranges and normalizing volume - we're one session removed from another down day with still-expanding ranges. Staying in wait mode again: holding ~65% cash buffer and existing trimmed positions unchanged, no new buys or sells today. Will continue monitoring for either (a) a genuine basing pattern - narrowing ranges, falling volume, 2+ up/flat sessions - to start redeploying incrementally, or (b) a fresh breakdown below the 4/7-4/8 lows on volume, which would push me to trim further toward a 75-80% cash floor.

April 9 close data shows an enormous, broad-based single-session rally across the entire basket on very heavy volume: MSFT +10.1%, AAPL +9.5%, GOOGL +9.5%, AVGO +9.4% off a 40% peak-to-trough range close, QCOM +15.2%, WMT +9.5%, ADP +6.5%, LIN +7.9%, PEP +3.8%, COST +6.2% - all reversing sharply off multi-week lows with volume still running well above average (AAPL 184M, MSFT 50M, QCOM 21M). This is a much stronger and more broad-based reversal signal than my prior stated trigger of '2-3 consecutive up/flat sessions with contracting ranges' - it's only one session and ranges are still wide, so it doesn't fully satisfy that mechanical rule. However, waiting for perfect confirmation risks missing a major low entirely, especially given the scale and breadth of this move (every name in the basket participated with double-digit intraday swings and closes near session highs). Compromise: deploying roughly 25% of the ~65% cash buffer (~$8,000 of $31,143 cash) in equal $800 tranches across all 10 existing positions, adding to conviction without going all-in. This keeps a large majority of cash (~23,000, still ~47% of NAV) in reserve in case this proves to be a bull-trap/dead-cat bounce within a larger downtrend. I will watch the next 1-2 sessions: if follow-through continues with narrowing ranges and volume normalizing, I'll deploy the remaining cash incrementally; if we see a sharp reversal back below the 4/7-4/8 lows on volume, I will stop deploying and consider trimming the new adds.

April 10 close shows a pullback from the huge April 9 rally across the basket (MSFT -2.4%, AAPL -4.2%, GOOGL -3.7%, QCOM -6.4%, WMT -1.9%, LIN -3.2%, ADP -0.8%, AVGO -6.9%, COST flat, PEP -1.0%), but critically: (1) volume declined meaningfully from the 4/9 spike (MSFT 38M vs 50M, AAPL 122M vs 184M, GOOGL 48M vs 70M, QCOM 15M vs 21M) - consistent with cooling off rather than fresh panic; (2) all names closed well above their 4/7-4/8 capitulation lows, holding the bulk of the 4/9 reversal gains (e.g. AAPL 190 vs 4/9 close 199 and 4/7 low 174.6; MSFT 381 vs 4/9 close 390 and 4/7 low 344.8). This looks like a normal one-day consolidation/give-back after an outsized single-session rally, not a breakdown - no name closed below its 4/9 open, and ranges, while still wide, are narrower than 4/9's. This is the first sign of the basing behavior I've been watching for (narrowing ranges + falling volume), though not yet the full 2-3 session confirmation. Continuing the incremental redeployment plan: another ~$800 equal tranche across all 10 existing positions (~$8,000 total, roughly matching the 4/10 tranche size), leaving still-substantial cash (~15,000, ~31% of NAV) as a buffer. Will keep watching: if the next 1-2 sessions show further range contraction and volume normalization, I'll continue deploying toward full allocation; if instead prices break back below the 4/7 lows on renewed volume expansion, I'll halt deployment and consider trimming the recent adds.

April 11 close confirms the basing pattern I've been tracking: after the 4/9 rally and 4/10 pullback, 4/11 posted a second consecutive up day (MSFT +1.9%, AAPL +4.1%, GOOGL +2.8%, QCOM +3.6%, WMT +2.4%, LIN +2.3%, ADP +2.5%, AVGO +5.6%, COST -0.1%, PEP +0.2%) with volume continuing to decline steadily across the basket (MSFT 24M vs 38M vs 50M peak; AAPL 87M vs 122M vs 184M; GOOGL 34M vs 48M vs 70M; QCOM 11M vs 15M vs 21M; ADP 2.2M vs 3.3M vs 3.5M). Daily ranges have also narrowed materially versus the 4/9 spike day. This is exactly the 2-3 session confirmation (higher lows, contracting ranges, falling volume) I set as my mechanical redeployment trigger, so continuing the incremental deployment with another ~$750 equal tranche across all 10 positions (~$7,500 total), bringing cash down to roughly 15% of NAV. Still keeping a meaningful buffer rather than going all-in, since ranges, while narrower, are still wider than pre-selloff norms and this is only 2 sessions of confirmation, not a fully established trend. Will continue deploying the remaining cash incrementally if the basing continues (narrowing ranges, volume near ~20-day average, no break below 4/7-4/8 lows); will halt and reassess if we see a fresh break below those lows on rising volume.

April 14 close data shows a more ambiguous session than the prior two: several names gapped up firmly at the open then faded significantly intraday before closing (MSFT open 393.22 -> close 387.81, essentially flat vs 4/11 close 388.45; AAPL open 211.44 -> close 202.52, only +2.2% vs prior close after a much stronger open; AVGO open 185.08 -> close 178.36, -2% vs prior close; QCOM roughly flat 139.19 vs 139.25 after opening at 142.75). This gap-and-fade pattern (strong opens giving back most/all gains intraday) is a mild caution signal versus the clean higher-lows/narrowing-range basing of 4/10-4/11, even though WMT, COST, PEP, LIN, ADP, GOOGL still closed solidly higher. Meanwhile my cash buffer is already at ~15.4% of NAV ($7,643 of $49,737), right at the target level I set in the 4/14 journal entry. Given the mixed/fading price action and having already reached my stated interim allocation target, I'm pausing further deployment today rather than continuing the incremental buy program - no trades. I'll resume adding if the next session shows clean follow-through (closes near highs, no intraday fade, contracting ranges) or if pullbacks find support well above the 4/7-4/8 lows on light volume. I'll consider trimming/de-risking if we get a fresh close below those lows on rising volume, or if the gap-fade pattern repeats with heavier volume (distribution signature).

April 15 close continues the mixed/consolidating pattern from 4/14 rather than resolving cleanly. Most positions closed modestly lower vs 4/14 (GOOGL -1.7%, PEP -2.7%, ADP -1.2%, WMT -0.8%, MSFT -0.5%, QCOM -0.4%, COST -0.2%, AAPL -0.2%) while LIN (+1.1%) and AVGO (+0.3%) ticked up. Volume continues to decline basket-wide (e.g. AAPL 51M vs 101M vs 184M peak; MSFT 17M vs 19M vs 50M; GOOGL 28M vs 30M vs 70M) and daily ranges remain contracted versus the 4/9 spike - consistent with ongoing basing/consolidation. Critically, no name is anywhere near the 4/7-4/8 capitulation lows (e.g. AAPL 202 vs 174.6 low, MSFT 386 vs 344.8 low, QCOM 139 vs 120.8 low, WMT 94 vs 79.8 low) - so no breakdown signal. But this also isn't the clean high-volume follow-through/closes-near-highs pattern I'm waiting for to resume deployment; it's a quiet drift-down on light volume, which I read as neutral rather than bullish or bearish. Staying with the pause-and-hold stance from 4/15: no trades today, keeping cash buffer at ~15.4% of NAV. Will resume incremental buying if I see a session with broad closes near intraday highs and volume ticking up (healthy demand), or if pullbacks stabilize well above the 4/7-4/8 lows with volume staying light. Will consider trimming if we get a fresh close below those lows on rising volume.

April 16 close shows a broader, sharper pullback than the recent drift: MSFT -3.7%, AAPL -3.9%, WMT -3.0%, AVGO -2.4%, QCOM -2.1%, PEP -1.9%, GOOGL -1.9%, ADP -1.3%, COST -0.9%, LIN -0.7% vs 4/15. This breaks below the tight 4/14-4/15 consolidation range on a modest volume uptick (AAPL 59.7M vs 51.3M, MSFT 22M vs 17.2M, WMT 22.2M vs 21.9M) - not a huge volume spike, but enough to flag this as more than quiet drift. However, all names remain comfortably above the 4/7-4/8 capitulation lows (AAPL 194.3 vs 174.6 low, MSFT 371.6 vs 344.8 low, QCOM 135.7 vs 120.8 low, WMT 91.2 vs 79.8 low, AVGO 174.6 vs 138.1 low), so my mechanical trim trigger (fresh close below those lows on rising volume) is not met. At the same time this is clearly not the closes-near-highs/volume-confirmation pattern needed to resume buying - it's the opposite, a broad red day. Given the mixed signal (breakdown of short-term range but no violation of the deeper support), I'm holding: no new buys (would be adding into weakness without confirmation) and no trims (no breach of the established support/capitulation lows). Cash buffer stays ~15.7% of NAV. Will resume buying on a session with broad closes near intraday highs and rising volume; will trim if 4/7-4/8 lows are breached on rising volume, or if this down-move extends 2+ more sessions with widening ranges (distribution signature).

No new closing data since 4/17 (4/18 was Good Friday market holiday), so this session's opening context matches what I already evaluated. 4/17 close vs 4/16 was mixed: COST +2.8%, PEP +1.9%, WMT +2.2%, AAPL +1.4%, LIN +0.9%, QCOM +0.7% advanced while MSFT -1.0%, GOOGL -1.4%, ADP -0.3%, AVGO -2.1% declined. Several names (MSFT, AVGO, ADP, GOOGL, QCOM) closed in the lower half of their intraday range rather than near highs, so this doesn't meet my bar for resuming buys (broad closes near highs with rising volume). At the same time, every holding remains comfortably above the 4/7-4/8 capitulation lows (AAPL 194 vs 174.6 low, MSFT 367.8 vs 344.8 low, QCOM 136.7 vs 120.8 low, WMT 93.2 vs 79.8 low, AVGO 171 vs 138.1 low), so the trim trigger isn't met either. Volume also wasn't notably elevated versus recent sessions. Holding cash buffer at ~15.7% of NAV, no trades. Will resume incremental buying on a session with broad closes near intraday highs and rising volume across the basket; will trim if capitulation lows are breached on rising volume.

4/21 close vs 4/17 continued the broader pullback: MSFT -2.4%, GOOGL -2.3%, ADP -2.8%, LIN -1.8%, AVGO -2.8%, COST -3.7%, WMT -09%, QCOM -0.4% declined while AAPL +ish flat/mixed, PEP flat. Intraday closes were mixed-to-weak: several names (MSFT, COST, ADP, LIN) closed in the lower half of their range, while AAPL and QCOM closed near the upper half - not the broad closes-near-highs pattern needed to resume buying. Volume was mixed too (some up modestly like ADP, COST, QCOM, PEP; others down like MSFT, AAPL, WMT, GOOGL, LIN) - no clear rising-volume confirmation either way. Critically, every holding remains comfortably above the 4/7-4/8 capitulation lows (AAPL 189.8 vs 174.6 low, MSFT 355.7 vs 344.8 low, QCOM 133.4 vs 120.8 low, WMT 91.3 vs 79.8 low, AVGO 161.6 vs 138.1 low, COST 943.0 vs 871.7 low), so the trim trigger isn't met. Staying in pause-and-hold mode: no trades, cash buffer ~16% of NAV. Will resume incremental buying on a session with broad closes near intraday highs and clearly rising volume across the basket; will trim if 4/7-4/8 lows are breached on rising volume.

4/22 close vs 4/21 delivered the broad rally I was waiting for: every core holding advanced 1.2%-3.4% (AAPL +3.4%, ADP +2.8%, WMT +2.6%, GOOGL +2.6%, LIN +2.4%, COST +2.2%, MSFT +2.1%, AVGO +2.0%, QCOM +1.9%, PEP +1.2%). Critically, closes were broadly near intraday highs across the whole basket (MSFT 366.8 vs 367.8 high, LIN 454.6 vs 455.3 high, QCOM 138.7 vs 139.1 high, AVGO 169.6 vs 170.5 high, GOOGL 151.5 vs 152.2 high, PEP 143.5 vs 144.3 high, WMT 94.9 vs 95.3 high) - the closes-near-highs pattern I set as my resume-buying trigger. Volume confirmation was partial/mixed (AAPL and GOOGL up meaningfully, others flat-to-down vs 4/21), so I'm not going all-in - deploying only a modest incremental tranche (~$3.4k, weighting AAPL/GOOGL/QCOM/LIN slightly higher given their stronger relative volume/strength) rather than fully redeploying the cash buffer. This still leaves roughly 8-9% cash buffer for further confirmation or a pullback opportunity. Will add more on continued closes-near-highs with clearer broad volume expansion; will pause/trim again if this reverses back below the 4/16-4/17 lows on rising volume.

4/23 close vs 4/22 was mixed, not a clean continuation of the 4/22 rally: AVGO +4.3%, GOOGL +2.6%, AAPL +2.4%, MSFT +2.1%, QCOM +1.2% advanced, but COST -0.3%, PEP -0.8%, LIN -1.4% declined, and ADP/WMT were roughly flat. Intraday positioning was also mixed - AVGO, GOOGL, AAPL, MSFT closed mid-to-upper range, but COST, LIN, QCOM closed in the lower half of their range near session lows. This doesn't meet my bar for a confident broad add (needs broad closes-near-highs with volume confirmation), but it's also nowhere near a trim trigger since every holding remains comfortably above the 4/7-4/8 capitulation lows. Cash buffer is already thin (~8.6% of NAV) after the 4/23 incremental tranche, so I'm comfortable holding here rather than chasing a mixed/inconclusive session. No trades. Will add more on a session with clear broad closes near highs and rising volume across the basket; will trim if 4/16-4/21 lows are breached on rising volume.

4/24 close vs 4/23 was a broad, volume-confirmed rally across most of the basket with closes near intraday highs: AAPL +1.8% (close 208.37 vs high 208.83), MSFT +3.5% (387.30 vs 388.45, volume up to 22.2M from 20.5M), GOOGL +2.5% (159.28 vs 159.59, volume surged to 45.9M from 31.1M), AVGO +6.4% (188.15 vs 188.57, volume up to 27.6M), QCOM +4.8% (147.21 vs 147.82), WMT +0.9% (95.84 vs 96.22), LIN +0.3%, ADP +0.3%, COST flat. This matches my resume-buying trigger (broad closes-near-highs with volume confirmation in several names), so I'm deploying a modest incremental tranche weighted toward AVGO/MSFT/GOOGL/QCOM/AAPL which showed the strongest price+volume combination. PEP was the exception: -4.9% on 2x normal volume (15.6M vs 7.8M), closing near session low (135.31 vs 134.53 low) and breaking decisively below its entire 4/14-4/23 range (prior lows 139.77-142.63) - this looks like a news-driven breakdown, not noise, so I'm trimming ~65% of the PEP position (20 of 30.6 units) rather than averaging down into a falling knife. Net effect: reduce single-name risk in the weakest holding, redeploy into the names confirming strength, keep cash buffer near ~9% of NAV for further flexibility. Will add more to the rally names on continued closes-near-highs with volume; will finish exiting PEP if it keeps making lower lows on volume, or reconsider re-adding if it stabilizes and reclaims the 142-143 area.

4/25 close vs 4/24 was mixed, not a clean broad rally: MSFT +1.2% (closed 391.85 vs 392.16 high, very tight to high) and AVGO +2.2% (192.31 vs 193.37 high) were strong, GOOGL +1.7% but closed well off its high (161.96 vs 166.10 high, weak), QCOM +0.9% near high, COST +0.2% near high, AAPL +0.4% modest. But ADP -0.9% closing near session low (291.76 vs 288.75 low), WMT -0.8% mid-range, LIN -0.3%, and critically PEP -1.4% making a fresh lower low (131.80, below the 4/24 crash low of 134.53) on still-elevated volume (11.5M vs ~7-8M normal, following the 15.6M breakdown day). This doesn't meet my broad-rally add trigger (mixed intraday positioning, volume confirmation fading on the winners like MSFT/AVGO vs 4/24), so no new buys today. PEP, however, continues to make lower lows on above-average volume exactly as I flagged as my exit-completion trigger in the 4/25 note - selling the remaining ~10.6 units to fully exit rather than let it keep bleeding. This raises cash buffer to roughly 12% of NAV, which I'm comfortable holding given the lack of a clean broad confirmation signal today. Will resume adding to MSFT/AVGO/QCOM/COST on a session with broad closes-near-highs AND volume expansion across the basket; will reconsider re-adding PEP only if it stabilizes and reclaims the 142-143 area on constructive volume.

4/28 close vs 4/25 was a quiet, mixed consolidation day, not a fresh trigger in either direction: MSFT -0.18%, GOOGL -0.83%, QCOM -0.63%, ADP +0.62%, AAPL +0.41%, COST +0.14%, WMT +0.14%, LIN -0.09%, AVGO +0.08%. Volumes broadly declined across the basket (MSFT 16.6M vs 19M avg, GOOGL 29.7M vs 45.9M prior day, AVGO 16.4M vs 21-27M prior days) consistent with digestion after the 4/24-4/25 rally rather than a new breakout or breakdown. No name is threatening its 4/16-4/21 lows, and no name is making a fresh volume-confirmed high either. This doesn't meet my add trigger (need broad closes-near-highs with volume expansion) nor my trim trigger (need broken support on rising volume), so holding all positions unchanged today. Cash buffer sits around 12% of NAV post PEP-exit, which I'm comfortable carrying through this low-conviction session. Will resume adding to MSFT/AVGO/QCOM/GOOGL/AAPL on a session with broad closes near highs and volume expansion; will trim if 4/16-4/21 lows are breached on rising volume.

4/29 close vs 4/28 was mixed-to-modestly-positive but not a clean broad rally: MSFT +0.74% (394.04 vs high 395.10, tight), AAPL +0.51% (211.21 vs high 212.24, tight), COST +1.34% (991.70 vs high 993.21, tight), WMT +0.86% (96.04 vs high 96.18, very tight), ADP +0.75%, LIN +0.58% - these six closed near session highs, constructive. But GOOGL -0.28%, AVGO -0.68%, QCOM -0.50% lagged, and volumes across the board remain below the 4/24-25 rally levels (MSFT 15M vs 22M peak, GOOGL 26.8M vs 45.9M peak, AVGO 14.6M vs 27.6M peak) - this looks like quiet continuation/digestion rather than a fresh volume-confirmed breakout. Doesn't meet my add trigger (need broad closes-near-highs AND volume expansion together) nor my trim trigger (no support breaks, nothing near 4/16-21 lows). Holding all positions unchanged again today, cash buffer ~12% of NAV. Will add to MSFT/AVGO/QCOM/GOOGL/AAPL on a session combining broad closes-near-highs with volume expansion; will trim if 4/16-21 lows are breached on rising volume.

4/30 close vs 4/29 delivered the broad-rally + volume-expansion combo I've been waiting for across most of the basket: MSFT +0.31% on 36.5M vol (vs 15M prior, near high 396.66/close 395.26), AAPL +0.61% on 52.3M (vs 36.8M, near high), COST +0.28% on 2.2M (vs 1.5M), LIN +0.59% on 2.7M (vs 1.2M), ADP +1.63% on 3.3M (vs 1.6M, strong breakout), AVGO +0.65% on 22.8M (vs 14.6M), QCOM +1.08% on 10.9M (vs 6.7M), WMT +1.26% on 21.6M (vs 12.7M, near high). All eight closed at or near session highs with volume roughly doubling vs the prior session - this is the confirmed broad breakout signal from my add trigger. GOOGL was the exception: -1.11% and lagging, so skipping it today pending its own confirmation. Also today is May 1 - the $50k monthly deposit landed, pushing cash to ~56% of NAV, well above my normal ~12% buffer, so this is a good session to deploy meaningfully into the confirmed breakout rather than a marginal add. Buying ~$5k each into MSFT/AAPL/COST/LIN/ADP/AVGO/QCOM/WMT, leaving cash buffer around 16% of NAV. Will reconsider adding GOOGL if it reclaims its highs with volume; will trim any of these if they break back below their 4/16-4/21 lows on rising volume.

5/1 close vs 4/30 was dominated by earnings-driven dispersion rather than a coherent basket signal: MSFT +7.6% on a huge gap (58.9M vol vs 36.5M prior) - clear earnings beat, no action needed since already held. AAPL +0.4%, GOOGL +1.6% (but on lower volume 30.2M vs 34.9M, not a breakout), COST +0.5%, WMT +0.2% - all quiet, no trigger either way. AVGO +2.5% continuing higher. LIN gapped down hard at the open (437 vs prior close 453, low 433) before recovering to 448.05 (-1.1%) - a scare but not a clean support break, volume only modestly elevated (2.54M vs 1.2-2.7M range), holding as-is for now. QCOM was the standout negative: -8.9% on 22.8M volume (vs 5-11M range recently), likely an earnings miss/guide-down, with today's low (134.87) dipping below the 4/17 low (135.71) though not quite breaching the 4/21 low (133.36).
